title: Impact of School Finance Reform on Math Test Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

The data structure clearly supports a DID design: we have treated vs. untreated schools (`treated`), pre vs. post reform periods (`post`), and their interaction (`treat_x_post`). The key causal parameter is the coefficient on `treat_x_post`, which captures the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) — the change in math test scores for reform-affected schools relative to unaffected schools, net of common time trends.

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of the reform, math test scores in treated and control schools would have followed the same trajectory over time. This is testable in pre-treatment periods if multiple pre-periods exist.

Additional assumptions:
- **No anticipation**: Schools did not change behavior before the reform was implemented.
- **No spillovers (SUTVA)**: The reform in treated schools did not affect outcomes in control schools.
- **Stable composition**: The school populations didn't change differentially due to the reform.

## 2. R Code

```r
# Load necessary libraries
library(fixest)
library(data.table)

# Read the data
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s35_data.csv")

# ============================================================
# Exploratory Data Analysis
# ============================================================
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
cat("Number of schools:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Number of periods:", length(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated schools:", sum(df[period == min(df$period)]$treated), "\n")
cat("Control schools:", sum(df[period == min(df$period)]$treated == 0), "\n\n")

# Group means
cat("=== Group Means ===\n")
group_means <- df[, .(mean_y = mean(y), sd_y = sd(y), n = .N), 
                   by = .(treated, post)]
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
y_t1_pre  <- group_means[treated == 1 & post == 0]$mean_y
y_t1_post <- group_means[treated == 1 & post == 1]$mean_y
y_t0_pre  <- group_means[treated == 0 & post == 0]$mean_y
y_t0_post <- group_means[treated == 0 & post == 1]$mean_y

did_manual <- (y_t1_post - y_t1_pre) - (y_t0_post - y_t0_pre)
cat("\nManual DID estimate:", round(did_manual, 4), "\n\n")

# ============================================================
# Main DID Regression
# ============================================================
cat("=== Model 1: Basic DID (OLS) ===\n")
model1 <- feols(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model1)

cat("\n=== Model 2: DID with School Fixed Effects ===\n")
model2 <- feols(y ~ post + treat_x_post | unit_id, data = df)
summary(model2)

cat("\n=== Model 3: DID with School and Period Fixed Effects (Two-Way FE) ===\n")
model3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(model3)

# ============================================================
# Robustness Checks
# ============================================================

# Robustness 1: Cluster standard errors at school level
cat("\n=== Robustness: Clustered Standard Errors at School Level ===\n")
model4 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
summary(model4)

# Robustness 2: Check parallel trends if multiple pre-periods exist
n_pre_periods <- length(unique(df[post == 0]$period))
if (n_pre_periods > 1) {
  cat("\n=== Parallel Trends Test (Event Study) ===\n")
  # Create relative time variable
  # Find the first post period
  first_post <- min(df[post == 1]$period)
  df[, rel_time := period - first_post]
  
  # Event study specification
  model_es <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, 
                     cluster = ~unit_id, data = df)
  summary(model_es)
  cat("\nPre-treatment coefficients should be insignificantly different from zero.\n")
} else {
  cat("\nOnly one pre-period available; cannot conduct event study for parallel trends.\n")
}

# Robustness 3: Placebo test - check treatment effect in pre-period only
if (n_pre_periods > 1) {
  cat("\n=== Placebo Test: Fake treatment in pre-period ===\n")
  pre_data <- df[post == 0]
  median_pre <- median(unique(pre_data$period))
  pre_data[, fake_post := as.integer(period > median_pre)]
  pre_data[, fake_treat_x_post := treated * fake_post]
  
  model_placebo <- feols(y ~ fake_treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                          cluster = ~unit_id, data = pre_data)
  summary(model_placebo)
  cat("Placebo coefficient should be insignificant.\n")
}

# ============================================================
# Summary of Results
# ============================================================
cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF RESULTS ===\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("ATT (Manual DID):", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")
cat("ATT (Basic OLS):", round(coef(model1)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("ATT (School FE):", round(coef(model2)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("ATT (Two-Way FE):", round(coef(model3)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("ATT (TWFE, clustered SE):", round(coef(model4)["treat_x_post"], 4), 
    " (SE:", round(se(model4)["treat_x_post"], 4), ")\n")
cat("========================================\n")

# Comparison table
cat("\n=== Regression Comparison Table ===\n")
etable(model1, model2, model3, model4,
       headers = c("Basic OLS", "School FE", "TWFE", "TWFE Clustered"),
       se.below = TRUE)
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected sign: Positive.** School finance reforms typically increase funding for disadvantaged schools, which should improve educational resources and consequently raise math test scores.

**Expected magnitude:** I expect the ATT coefficient on `treat_x_post` to be in the range of **0.1 to 0.5 standard deviations**. In the education literature, policy interventions that increase school funding tend to produce effect sizes in the range of 0.05–0.30 SD for test scores. Given that this is a simulated dataset designed to illustrate a clear effect, the coefficient may be on the larger side (0.2–0.5 SD).

**Robustness expectations:**
- The estimate should be relatively stable across specifications (OLS, school FE, TWFE), with school fixed effects reducing residual variance and tightening standard errors.
- Clustered standard errors will likely be slightly larger than heteroskedasticity-robust SEs, reflecting within-school correlation.
- If multiple pre-periods exist, event study coefficients should show no significant pre-trends (validating parallel trends) and a clear jump at or after the reform date.
- The placebo test should yield a null result, confirming no spurious effects in the pre-period.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: We compare changes in math test scores over time between schools affected by the reform and those that were not.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The reform led to a decrease in math test scores.
